title: Willow and the Lost Scarf
markdown:
Willow was a fluffy wolf pup, her fur the colour of warm honey, and her eyes sparkled like tiny amber beads. She loved chasing butterflies that flitted like painted jewels and sniffing bushes that smelled like secrets. But her absolute favourite thing? Her bright red scarf. It was not just any scarf. It was knitted from the fluffiest wool, warm and soft, like a hug from the sun itself. And it smelled faintly, wonderfully, of ripe blueberries. Every morning Willow would stretch out her little wolfy legs and unwrap herself from her cozy den, her paws searching for her red scarf. It was her special signal for a good day.

But this morning was different. Willow stretched, yawned a big wide puppy yawn that showed off her tiny pink tongue, and reached for her scarf. Her paw met empty air. Her little ears drooped a tiny bit. "Huh?" Her voice was still sleepy and confused. She wiggled out of her warm mossy bed, sniffing here and there with her damp little nose. Nothing. No bright red fuzz. No blueberry scent. A tiny tremor ran through her whiskers. A little wobble started in her tummy, like a tiny tickly cloud making her feel not quite sunshine-y. It felt a bit like when she tried to reach the highest branch of the berry bush, only this was a tummy feeling.

Just then a cheerful squeak, squeak announced her best friend, Minty the guinea pig. Minty was round and jolly, like a little furry ball of sunshine, with the most splendidly twitchy whiskers you ever did see. "What is wrong, Willow? You look as if you have lost your favourite giggle."

"My scarf," whimpered Willow, her lower lip quivering just a smidge. "My beautiful fuzzy blueberry-smelling scarf is gone." She wriggled her nose, trying to sniff out the missing treasure, but only the fresh morning dew greeted her.

Minty’s nose twitched with determination. "Gone? Oh dear. But do not worry, Willow. We will find it. We are the bestest friends, and we can find anything. Together." And just like that, Minty was looking at the ground, her little nose practically touching the dewdrops. "Look. A muddy pawprint. It is too small for you, Willow. See? And it is all squishy. Someone else has been here."

Willow peered down, her amber eyes wide. Indeed, a little muddy print sat right by her doorstep, a perfect miniature boot shape pressed into the soft earth. It was not a big stompy pawprint like her daddy’s, but a small neat one. Willow, feeling a tiny bit less wobbly in her tummy and a lot more determined, took a deep breath that puffed out her fluffy chest. "Okay, Minty. Let us follow it. We will be detectives."

And so they did. The little pawprint led them out of the den, through the dewy grass that tickled Willow’s paws, and past the wobbly daisies. The daisies, with their bright yellow centres and white petals, seemed to lean over as they went by. "Heehee. Looking for something?" they whispered in their daisy voices, their petals rustling like tiny silken dresses. Willow shook her head, her ears flopping slightly. "My scarf." They hopped and scurried, Willow’s ears swiveling this way and that, catching the faintest rustle of leaves, while Minty’s nose twitched with every scent carried on the gentle breeze: the sweet smell of clover, and the soft damp earth squishing beneath their paws.

They even asked a buzzy bee, who was very busy with a plump purple flower. The bee, its wings a blur of iridescent light, hummed a busy tune. "Buzz buzz? Oh, hello there. Nectar is so yummy today. Sorry, cannot stop. Buzz buzz?" hummed the bee, zipping away with a little zing toward another blossom, completely focused on its sweet mission.

"Hmm," said Minty, her whiskers drooping a little. "That bee did not see it either. Maybe it is too high up for bees to notice." Willow felt that tickly cloud of worry return, a little bigger this time. What if her scarf was lost forever in the big wide meadow? What if it had tumbled into a secret hidey-hole?

Just then they rounded a patch of tall whispering reeds. The meadow was quiet again, save for the soft hum of insects and the gentle sigh of the wind through the reeds. Willow took a deep breath, breathing in the sweet damp air, and looked up at the big blue sky. It was so vast, and the fluffy white clouds drifted like lazy sheep. For a moment she just stood there, her ears twitching, taking it all in.

Ahead, in a sunny grassy clearing bathed in warm golden light, was Gary the Goat. Gary was a big goat, with long curved horns that gleamed in the sun, and he was happily munching on a particularly tasty-looking patch of clover, its leaves feeling cool and crisp between his teeth. And draped right over his long curved horns was Willow’s bright red fuzzy scarf. It looked like a very cheerful, very fuzzy crown.

Gary was a very honest goat, you see. He loved telling the truth, but he was also a little bit forgetful, especially when his tummy was rumbling for yummy things. As Willow and Minty tiptoed closer, their hearts thumping like little drums, Gary looked up from his clover feast. "Baaaaa?" he bleated, his chewing slowing down, his big gentle eyes blinking slowly. He had a bit of green clover stuck to his chin.

"Gary, Gary." Willow barked, a little squeak in her voice, but no longer scared. "That is my scarf. My bright red fuzzy blueberry scarf."

Gary blinked his big gentle eyes. He looked at the red fuzz draped so cozily over his horns, then back at Willow. "Oh. This? I found it. It was lying on the ground, right by that big rock. It looked so bright and soft, and I thought it was the most comfortable place to put my snack. Like a special fuzzy holder for extra-delicious leaves." He let out a little giggle that sounded like pebbles tumbling down a gentle hill.

Willow giggled too. It was such a Gary thing to do. Gary carefully lowered his head, his horns tilting just so. The scarf, still smelling faintly of blueberries and feeling as soft as ever, slid gently onto the soft grass between them. "Here you go, Willow. It was very comfy for my snacks, but I suppose it is yours." He nudged it forward with his nose.

Willow nudged the scarf with her nose, a wave of happiness washing over her. It was safe. It was right here. She had not been too scared to follow the pawprint, and she had found her scarf. She carefully picked it up, her heart feeling full and warm, like a little bird singing in her chest. "Thank you, Gary. And thank you, Minty, for being so brave and helping me search."

Minty squeaked happily, wiggling her whiskers with pride. Gary gave a big happy baa and then, with a friendly nod, went back to his clover, already thinking about his next delicious mouthful. Willow wrapped her bright red fuzzy scarf around her neck. It felt like a warm hug, and today it felt even better because she had gone on an adventure to find it. The sun shone down, painting the meadow in shades of gold and green, and the scent of blueberries wafted gently around her. The scarf was lovely. The meadow, having given it back, kept on being a meadow.
